summary: Attacked part 3 of the Representation theory area — CompactGroups, LieGroups, LieHighestWeight, SpinRepresentations and ZigzagPreprojective, 46 stages — on four heads, with parts 1 and 2 read for duplication. One finding, medium: RootSystems and LieHighestWeight disclaim the weight-lattice apparatus in opposite directions using the same words, which is the most plausible root cause of the confirmed medium finding RT-AREA-representations-1/1. The library-boundary head is clean and unusually well documented — both roadmaps that make checkable claims about Mathlib are right, including CompactGroups' reproducible negative search. Duplication is clean: SpinRepresentations and part 2's SchurWeyl are complementary by explicit design, and ZigzagPreprojective's preprojective algebras are different objects from QuiverRepresentations' preprojective modules. The stage graph matches atlas norms.
checked: Every stage of all five roadmaps, with its document: CompactGroups 7, LieGroups 10, LieHighestWeight 10, SpinRepresentations 10, ZigzagPreprojective 9 — 46 in all. Declared roadmap-level prerequisites: CompactGroups (OrthogonalL2Bases, LieGroups), LieHighestWeight (LieGroups, RootSystems), SpinRepresentations (ClassicalGroups, LieHighestWeight, RootSystems); LieGroups and ZigzagPreprojective declare none.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed: none of the 43 papers this session has reviewed routes to any of these five roadmaps. This completes the area's trio — I verified part 1's red team (REV-RT-AREA-representations-1) and wrote part 2's (RT-AREA-representations-2) — which is the cross-part reading PROTOCOL section 17 asks each part to do, and is what produced the finding below.

That part 1's fix points somewhere real, since its target roadmap sits in this part. RT-AREA-representations-1/1 asked ClassicalGroups to cite LieHighestWeight for the abstract Weyl dimension formula; LieHighestWeight Layer 6 is 'the Weyl character, dimension, and Kostant formulas' and states it explicitly: 'The Weyl dimension formula. Specializing at the trivial character, dim L(λ) = ∏_{α>0} ⟨λ+ρ, α^∨⟩ / ⟨ρ, α^∨⟩'. The fix is sound.

The library boundary, target by target, on the two roadmaps that make checkable claims about Mathlib — the head that produced the model-theory area's sharpest finding. Both claims hold at the pin. SpinRepresentations says 'Mathlib has a substantial Clifford-algebra library and, unusually, already has the Pin and Spin groups', and names pinGroup, spinGroup, orthogonalGroup, specialOrthogonalGroup and equivExterior: all five exist, pinGroup and spinGroup in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/SpinGroup.lean, orthogonalGroup and specialOrthogonalGroup in LinearAlgebra/UnitaryGroup.lean, equivExterior in CliffordAlgebra/Inversion.lean. CompactGroups makes a reproducible negative claim — 'What Mathlib does not have is the theory that connects them: the Peter-Weyl theorem itself (a search for PeterWeyl/matrixCoeff in Mathlib returns nothing)' — and both searches return zero files, so the theorem is correctly planned rather than duplicated. No layer in the part plans what the library already has.

Duplication against part 2, on the pair the vocabulary flags: ZigzagPreprojective against QuiverRepresentations. Different objects under a shared adjective. ZigzagPreprojective is titled 'Zigzag, preprojective, and Ginzburg algebras' and plans zigzag algebras, quadratic and Koszul duality, 2-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebras, Calabi-Yau completions, A-infinity deformations and spherical twists — preprojective *algebras* — while QuiverRepresentations' single mention of the word is 'the preprojective/preinjective (n, n+1), (n+1, n)' dimension vectors of Auslander-Reiten theory, i.e. preprojective *modules*. ZigzagPreprojective is also careful about exactly this hazard, its summary undertaking to build its chain 'without identifying objects which agree only after a duality, a completion, or transfer of an A-infinity structure'.

Duplication against part 2, on the pair I had already settled from the other side: SpinRepresentations against SchurWeyl. Complementary by explicit design, SpinRepresentations' summary stating that spin representations are 'the one part of the finite-dimensional representation theory of the classical groups that the tensor-power engine cannot reach ... for the orthogonal series this is false'. It declares ClassicalGroups, LieHighestWeight and RootSystems as prerequisites.

The stage graph and status, calibrated against the atlas rather than against the sibling part. All 46 stages have empty `requires` and carry status 'unknown'. Atlas-wide, 669 of 1962 stages have empty `requires` (34 per cent) and 656 carry status 'unknown' (33 per cent), the only other value being 'needs_source_decomposition'. Within norms; prerequisites are recorded at roadmap level, as in part 2.

A note on a path that is easy to get wrong for whoever works here next: ZigzagPreprojective's roadmap id is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ZigzagPreprojective, not under .../RepresentationTheory/ like the area's other members, and its document is at content/tau-ceti/ZigzagPreprojective/README.md rather than content/tau-ceti/RepresentationTheory/. Its atlas record also carries readme: null while that document exists.

How the single finding was graded, recorded because it changed twice under checking. It first looked like a high-severity ownership gap in which nothing builds the weight lattice, since RootSystems and LieHighestWeight each disclaim it and assign it to the other, and LieHighestWeight rules out the escape that both defer to the library ('not in Mathlib as such'). Reading one level further showed LieHighestWeight does construct it — 'a named milestone constructs it as such, proves the roots lie in it, exhibits ρ (the half-sum of positive roots) as an element of it' — while reusing the abstract lattice and Weyl action from RootSystems. Nothing is unowned, so the finding is a terminological collision rather than a gap, and it is filed at medium rather than low only because its consequence is documented rather than hypothetical.

findings.claim: Two roadmaps disclaim the weight-lattice apparatus in opposite directions, naming the same objects in nearly the same words, so each document read alone says the other builds it. RootSystems' scope boundary sends the weight and root lattices, the fundamental weights, dominant integral weights and rho to LieHighestWeight; LieHighestWeight's 'What Mathlib already has' section sends the root/weight lattices, fundamental weights, rho, the dominance API and the Weyl action on the weight lattice back to RootSystems, saying 'we consume them from there'. Nothing is in fact unowned — LieHighestWeight does construct the integral weight lattice and rho in the Lie-theoretic setting, and reuses the abstract lattice from RootSystems — so the two notes are disclaiming different things under one name. The defect is the collision itself, and it is not hypothetical: it is the most plausible root cause of the confirmed medium finding RT-AREA-representations-1/1, where ClassicalGroups cited RootSystems for the Weyl dimension and character formulas, exactly the apparatus RootSystems' boundary sends away. Fixing only ClassicalGroups' citation leaves the trap in place for the next roadmap that reads either scope note.
findings.evidence: RootSystems README lines 45-51: 'Scope boundary. This roadmap stops at the root system, its Weyl group, chambers, and the classification. The weight and root lattices, the coweight and coroot lattices, the fundamental weights, dominant integral weights, and `rho` - the lattice apparatus that the Weyl character and dimension formulas run on - are **not** built here; they belong to [the highest-weight roadmap](../LieHighestWeight/README.md), which layers them on top of the chambers and the Weyl-group action supplied here.' LieHighestWeight README lines 165-167: 'The **root/weight lattices, fundamental weights, `rho`, the dominance API, and the Weyl action on the weight lattice** are **not** in Mathlib as such; they are the province of `../RootSystems/README.md`, and we consume them from there.' Line 202 repeats it: 'These, and the root/weight lattices, are the province of' RootSystems. What resolves the apparent gap, and shows the collision is terminological, is LieHighestWeight lines 114-119: 'The **integral weight lattice** `X` is therefore a Z-submodule of `Module.Dual K H`, **not** a K-subspace; a named milestone constructs it as such, proves the roots lie in it, exhibits `rho` (the half-sum of positive roots) as an element of it, and shows the coroot pairings land in Z. The Z-module structure of `X` and the Weyl action on it are shared with `../RootSystems/README.md`; we reuse the abstract lattice and do not rebuild it.' The downstream consequence is RT-AREA-representations-1/1, confirmed in REV-RT-AREA-representations-1.
findings.fix: Make each scope note say which sense it means, leaving the division of labour as it stands, since the division itself is sound. In RootSystems' boundary, say that the concrete weight-lattice apparatus — fundamental weights, dominant integral weights, rho as an element of the integral weight lattice, and the dominance API — is built in LieHighestWeight, while the abstract lattice object and the Weyl action on it are supplied here and reused there. In LieHighestWeight's 'What Mathlib already has' section, replace 'are the province of ../RootSystems/README.md, and we consume them from there' with a statement matching its own lines 114-119: the abstract lattice and Weyl action come from RootSystems, and the integral weight lattice X, rho as an element of it, and the dominance API are constructed here. Cross-reference the two notes so that a reader arriving at either finds the same division.
